زَامِلٌ , applied to a horse or similar beast, (K, TA,) or to a wild ass, (A' Obeyd, TA,) That is as though he limped, by reason of his briskness, or sprightliness. (A' Obeyd, K, TA.) [Hence, app., the name of] The horse of Mo'áwiyeh Ibn-Mirdás Es-Sulamee. (K.) ―
-b2- Also One who follows (↓ يَزْمُلُ , [in the CK يُزَمِّلُ,] i. e. يَتْبَعُ,) another. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
